annotationRationale: The central step connects divisibility of a square to its prime factors. Counting multiples and comparing candidate squares complete the argument. The supplied methods all use this same short route.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independently, 5 divides n² exactly when it divides n. The positive eligible roots are 5,10,...,40 because 40²<2023<45². There are 8 squares, agreeing with choice A and the key. No figure or statement contradiction.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2023_AMC_10A_Q03 / count-square-roots was independently verified and retained. LIVE and Random Math give the same root-counting route. Another method would add little to this short calculation.
review.annotationCheck: Prime-factor exponent structure is appropriately assessed. Multiples and square-root bracketing are appropriate support concepts; no contextual IDs are needed.
review.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Squaring doubles prime exponents, proving the divisibility equivalence. The eight listed positive multiples of 5 exhaust the possibilities, exclude zero, and yield distinct squares. The strict upper bound correctly excludes 45²=2025.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The explanation reuses the credited project method amc/2023_AMC_10A_Q03#count-square-roots for the identical question. Both inherited reference IDs, live-reference-2023_AMC_10A_Q03 and randommath-reference-2023_AMC_10A_Q03, are retained. The source-informed-original basis and nonofficial attribution are accurate; reuse of the supplied project prose is permitted.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why counting roots helps, the prime-exponent argument supplies the key implication, and the boundary comparison makes the enumeration reconstructible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All three IDs fit: math:prime-factorization supplies the decisive implication, cnm_p153 supplies the multiples, and cnm_079 supplies the implicit square-root bracketing.
